headlines.title: Seahawks land Quenton Nelson from the Colts
headlines.summary: Seattle acquired eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from Indianapolis for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The Colts went 2–5 and fired general manager Chris Ballard last week, which set off the trade speculation. Nelson is one of four offensive players since the 1970 merger to make the Pro Bowl in each of his first eight seasons, alongside Hall of Famers Franco Harris, Barry Sanders and Joe Thomas. The 4–3 Seahawks are adding a line upgrade to an offence that is already strong.
headlines.whyItMatters: Seattle sit just outside the NFC seeds at 4–3, and a stronger line helps them in a tight race. For the Colts, the picks are the start of a rebuild.

headlines.title: Colts send DeForest Buckner back to the 49ers
headlines.summary: Indianapolis traded three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco for a 2027 fourth-round pick. Buckner, 32, is in the final year of his deal and would be an unrestricted free agent after the season. This is a return to San Francisco for Buckner, who was the 49ers' 2016 first-round pick.
headlines.whyItMatters: The 49ers are 6–1 and the NFC's No. 2 seed, so adding pass rush is a real push for the playoffs. The Colts are gathering picks for next year.

headlines.title: Seahawks slow down the Chiefs

headlines.whyItMatters: Kansas City are still 5–1 and first in the AFC, so the result says more about Seattle's defence than about the Chiefs' season. It also moves Seattle to 4–3 and keeps them in the NFC hunt.

contextCard.title: How NFL injury designations work
contextCard.body: Teams list players as Out, Doubtful, Questionable or Probable before games. Out means the player will not play. headlines.title: Thunder lose two starters to injury but stay unbeaten
headlines.summary: Jalen Williams suffered a leg fracture and had to be stretchered off the court on Sunday night. Cason Wallace has a torn labrum and needs surgery. Oklahoma City have not put a timeline on either, but Yahoo says history suggests neither will play again this season. Despite it, the Thunder beat Phoenix 125–114 and remain 4–0.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Thunder are the West's No. 2 team with a 4–0 start, and they're now shifting toward offence without their two starters. The West race just got more open.

headlines.title: Jaren Jackson Jr. out at least six weeks for Utah
headlines.summary: Jackson tore the MCL in his right knee in Monday's home loss to Memphis, and the Jazz will re-evaluate him in six weeks. Sources told ESPN the timeline is six to eight weeks. Lauri Markkanen also left that game with a sprained right wrist and is listed as day-to-day. Jackson was acquired before last season's deadline in a deal that cost Utah three first-round picks.
headlines.whyItMatters: Utah are 1–3 and 13th in the West, and losing two bigs this early makes the rotation thin.

headlines.title: Heat start 0–4 with Giannis and Adebayo struggling

headlines.whyItMatters: A fourth straight loss makes Miami's early season a real problem. The question is how the new Giannis-Adebayo pairing works.

headlines.title: Lakers ownership sale is done, but uncertainty remains
headlines.summary: Mark Walter agreed to take over the Lakers after three days of secret talks. ESPN reports the deal has reignited arguments among the six Buss siblings. The Lakers are 3–0, and Luka Doncic scored 52 in a 132–123 win over Utah.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Lakers are off to a strong start, but the ownership changes will matter for the club's direction beyond this season.
